prompt.context: Our client is a large national health care payer (health insurance company, think Aetna) exploring the launch of a new disease management (DM) program to better serve its 5 million members. The idea is to hire and train a team of Health Coaches to specialize in a single disease area (e.g., heart disease, diabetes, etc). Each Coach will manage a portfolio of patients to reduce the costs of overall health expenditures (e.g., reminders to take drugs, provide limited medical advice, suggested diet, etc). Studies show that once a month contact with each patient reduces health spending by 5%, on average.
prompt.question: Should our client launch the program? If so, what steps should it take?

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive landscape like?
clarifying_info.a: With spiraling health care costs, the industry is under pressure to innovate. Assume client is first to market. Past attempts to purely automate DM have yielded minimal savings.

clarifying_info.q: How do the Health Coaches operate?
clarifying_info.a: All activity is conducted remotely via phone/email. Typical profile is a registered nurse that wants to work from home. It is difficult to actually reach patients, so Coaches can contact 8 members per day (assume 25 days per month).

clarifying_info.q: What are the costs per Health Coach?
clarifying_info.a: Annual cost per Coach: $60K salary plus 20% for other (training, benefits, laptop, etc). There are no other program costs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the 5% savings figure based on?
clarifying_info.a: Studies show that once-a-month contact with each patient reduces health spending by 5%, on average.

exhibits.title: Client's member segmentation by health condition
exhibits.shows: A chart segmenting the client's 5 million members by plan type (Group, Individual, 65+) and by health condition (including diabetics and other disease areas), showing the proportion of each segment and the share with each condition.
exhibits.data: 65+ segment = 20% of members (1MM); Individual segment = 20% of members (1MM); Group segment = 60% of members (3MM). Within 65+: ~40% are diabetic. Note: 65+ members are Medicare Advantage patients, premiums funded by government.

exhibits.title: Average cost data (Per Member Per Month)
exhibits.shows: A table showing average Per Member Per Month (PMPM) medical costs by segment, and a multiplier for diabetic members relative to the segment average.
exhibits.data: Individual: avg PMPM $150; Group: avg PMPM $100; 65+: avg PMPM $300. Average Diabetic cost = 4x the segment's avg PMPM for all segments.

framework: Program Savings: identify which customer segment and disease area drives the highest per-member costs, then quantify the 5% cost reduction for that population
Program Costs: calculate annual cost per Health Coach (salary + benefits/other) and determine portfolio capacity (members per Coach) to derive cost per member served
Profitability: compare savings per Coach portfolio vs. cost per Coach across segments to determine break-even and profit
Risks & Next Steps: assess whether assumptions hold, consider competitive response, regulatory/liability issues, and recommend a phased launch

questions.prompt: Which member segment and disease area should the client focus on first, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 1 to segment members. 65+ (Medicare) patients are the sickest (highest PMPM), making them the best candidates for DM — the 5% savings will have the biggest dollar impact. Within 65+, diabetics make up the largest share of sick members and, as a chronic behavioral disease, Type 2 diabetes is most amenable to coaching. Candidate should conclude: focus on 65+ diabetics first.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum patient portfolio size for one Health Coach?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply daily contact capacity by working days per month to get the maximum portfolio size.

math.setup: 8 contacts/day x 25 days/month = max monthly contacts = max portfolio size (since each patient is contacted once a month)

questions.prompt: What is the annual cost per Health Coach?
How many 65+ diabetics are in the client's membership?
questions.guidance: Use the segment share from Exhibit 1 and the diabetic proportion within 65+.

math.setup: Total members x 65+ segment % x diabetic % within 65+

questions.prompt: What are the annual savings generated by one Health Coach's portfolio of 65+ diabetics?
questions.guidance: Use Exhibit 2 to get average PMPM for 65+, apply the 4x diabetic factor, multiply by 5% savings rate, scale to 12 months and 200 patients.

math.setup: Avg PMPM for 65+ x diabetic factor x savings rate x 12 months x portfolio size

questions.prompt: Is the Health Coach program profitable for the 65+ segment? What about Individual and Group?
questions.guidance: Compare savings per Coach to cost per Coach. For Individual: PMPM is $150 (half of 65+), so savings are half = $72K, which equals cost — break-even. For Group: PMPM is $100 (1/3 of 65+), so savings ~$48K, less than $72K cost — a loss.

math.setup: Profit per Coach = Savings per Coach - Cost per Coach
math.answer: 65+ segment: $72,000 profit per Coach per year (2x return). Individual: break-even. Group: loss.

questions.prompt: What is the total potential annual profit if the program is fully deployed across all 65+ diabetics?
questions.guidance: Divide total 65+ diabetics by portfolio size to get number of Coaches needed, then multiply by profit per Coach.

math.setup: (Total 65+ diabetics / portfolio size) x profit per Coach

brainstorming.prompt: There are 650K Group diabetics left uncoached. Is there a way to make the Group segment profitable?

categories.name: More efficient DM delivery
ideas: Coaching at the workplace to improve reach rates
Bi-monthly contact instead of monthly to handle more patients per Coach
Automated correspondence (apps, text reminders) to supplement or replace some live contact

categories.name: Additional revenue sources
ideas: Employers (Group plan sponsors) might pay a fee for the program given productivity/absenteeism benefits
Government subsidies or grants for preventive care programs
Bundled payment or shared-savings arrangements with employers

categories.name: Target higher-responding members
ideas: Since 5% is an average, identify and target Group members whose savings would be well above 5%
Use claims data to find highest-cost Group diabetics where the dollar impact is larger

recommendation: Client should launch the Health Coaching program, initially focusing on Type 2 diabetes in the 65+ Medicare segment
The 65+ diabetic segment yields $72K profit per Coach per year (2x return on cost), and total program profit is ~$144M/year across 2,000 Coaches
The Individual diabetic segment is break-even and may be worth including for customer retention and moral rationale
The Group diabetic segment is loss-making at current parameters and should not be included in the initial launch
risks: The 5% average cost reduction assumption may not hold across all patients — a pilot is needed to validate
Coach portfolio capacity of 200 assumes 8 contacts/day are achievable; actual reach rates may be lower
Regulatory and liability risks associated with remote medical advice from Health Coaches
Competitive response once program is proven — first-mover advantage is temporary
next_steps: Launch a pilot program to validate key assumptions (5% savings rate, Coach capacity, patient engagement)
Scale to the full 65+ diabetic segment ($144M/year opportunity)
Analyze whether Individual segment merits inclusion despite break-even economics
Develop a plan to address the Group segment: employer co-pay model, higher-efficiency delivery, or targeted high-cost member outreach
Explore selling the Health Coach service to other payers as an external product (with appropriate pricing and regulatory review)
